Bioregulators in Canada — What Every Listing Shows

Bioregulators are the family of very short peptides — most are two to four residues — that came out of the St Petersburg Institute of Bioregulation and Gerontology under Vladimir Khavinson. Each was isolated from, or designed to match, a peptide fraction of one tissue: epitalon (AEDG) from the pineal gland, cartalax (AEDL) from cartilage, vesugen (KED) from vascular tissue, livagen (KEDA) from liver, pinealon (EDR) from brain cortex. The research literature on them is largely Russian-language and partly indexed in English, and the product pages are explicit about that.

The category also holds the longer complexes studied in the same tradition — cerebrolysin and thymulin — and the N-acetyl form of epitalon, which is a different compound with its own stability profile, not an alternative name.

Short peptides are easy to identify and hard to adulterate, and every lot here carries an independent certificate with purity and measured content against its batch code; sequence, CAS number and formula are published on each page. Where a compound’s evidence base is limited to its originating group, the page says so. Supplied strictly as laboratory research materials, shipped within Canada.

records.title: Vesugen
records.description:
Vesugen is the tripeptide Lys-Glu-Asp, studied in research on vascular endothelium and age-related vascular change.
Experimental work examines endothelial cell proliferation and vasoprotective endpoints under controlled conditions.
Overview
Vesugen is a three-residue peptide investigated within the vascular arm of the short-peptide bioregulator literature. Published work has examined molecular aspects of KED activity in atherosclerosis and restenosis models, and epigenetic aspects of peptidergic regulation of vascular endothelial cell proliferation during ageing.
More recent review work places the peptide within research on the senescence-associated secretory phenotype in cardiovascular cells.
History
Vesugen was characterized as the vascular-directed member of a family of short peptides differing by one or two residues.
Research from the 2010s focused on endothelial proliferation and vascular ageing, connecting the compound to the inflammaging literature.
Research
Research into the KED sequence focuses on vascular endothelial proliferation and vasoprotective endpoints during ageing. Frameworks evaluate atherosclerosis and restenosis models, epigenetic regulation, and senescence-associated signaling in cardiovascular cells.

records.title: Livagen
records.description:
Livagen is the tetrapeptide Lys-Glu-Asp-Ala, studied in research on hepatic tissue models and on chromatin activation in lymphocytes.
Experimental work examines tissue-specific short-peptide activity in cultures from animals and donors of different ages.
Overview
Livagen is among the better-documented short peptide bioregulators. Published studies have examined chromatin decondensation in lymphocytes from older donors, protein-synthesis rhythms in hepatocyte cultures, and digestive-enzyme activity in rodent models.
That work sits within a broader research model in which short peptides are proposed to act on heterochromatin and gene expression rather than through classical receptor pharmacology.
History
Livagen was characterized as one of a series of tissue-directed tetrapeptides in the Russian peptide-bioregulator programme, with an emphasis on hepatic tissue.
Subsequent research extended into lymphocyte chromatin studies, which became some of the most cited work in this compound class.
Research
Research into Livagen focuses on chromatin activation in ageing lymphocytes and on tissue-specific effects in hepatic culture models. Frameworks evaluate heterochromatin decondensation, protein-synthesis rhythms, and enzyme activity under controlled in vitro and preclinical conditions.

records.title: Crystagen
records.description:
Crystagen is a short synthetic peptide of the bioregulator class, supplied as the tripeptide Glu-Asp-Pro and studied in research on immune-tissue models.
Published work addresses the sequence in the context of spleen and immune-cell ageing rather than the trade name.
Overview
Crystagen sits within the family of short regulatory peptides investigated for tissue-directed activity in immune research models. Studies have examined immunoprotective activity of short peptides in spleen tissue during ageing, and the broader role of such peptides in directing cell differentiation.
The compound-specific literature is thin. Most available research addresses the short-peptide class collectively rather than this sequence in isolation.
History
Crystagen emerged from the Russian peptide-bioregulator research programme, which characterized a series of tissue-directed short peptides intended to model endogenous regulatory fragments.
Published investigation has remained largely confined to immune-tissue culture and ageing models.
Research
Research relevant to Crystagen centers on short-peptide immunoprotective activity in spleen tissue during ageing and on peptide regulation of cell differentiation. Reference support is thin relative to better-characterized compounds.
